agree.reason: Accepting the staff's stock numbers and asking for a 3-fish limit or shorter season makes this captain more credible than most, but the draft offers nothing the commission can check, such as the 2016-on trip logs or the reporting-app trial, so a commissioner who trusts staff has little reason to vote against them.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'every boat out of business' claim, but 'charter boats land the least flounder in this state' and the claim that private anglers only get 'a shorter day on the water' go beyond the 9%/80% figures, and $80,000 over three years ignores the recovery after 2016.

works_the_facts.reason: The 'almost one in five' drop and the roughly $27,000-a-season loss are fair figures from the brief, but the three-year total multiplies the worst year instead of following the 2016 recovery, the survey is left as raw counts rather than 59%, and the 70% of this season already booked goes unused.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the 2016 drop and the partial recovery to 155 and notes that bookings never fully came back, but then projects a full three years at the worst-year loss, which contradicts the trend it just described.

qualification.reason: The only condition is 'if a 3-fish limit or a shorter season can get the stock where it needs to be', with no number, date, or check, and it leaves out the commitments (trip logs, app trial) that would give the commission something to verify.

objections.reason: It heads off the stock-science objection and the 'you recovered last time' objection, but it never addresses whether a 3-fish limit meets staff's target, and the 9% share cuts both ways without comment.

fit.reason: At about 330 words it is roughly a two-minute spoken comment in plain sentences, but it never gives the speaker's name or boat, which a public comment normally states.
